claim: Vgll4l is strongly expressed at gastrula stage in LRO progenitors.
source: By this approach, we identified Vgll4l, a TcoF member of the Vestigial like four family, which is strongly expressed at gastrula stage in LRO progenitors (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Vgll4 family members are TcoFs known to function mainly through interaction with TEA domain DNA-binding family of transcription factors (TEAD).
source: Vestigial like family members are TcoFs known to function mainly through the interaction with TEA domain DNA-binding family of transcription factors (TEAD) (Deng and Fang, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Deng and Fang, 2018.

claim: TEADs are the DNA binding TFs to which the TcoFs Yap and Taz bind to activate expression of their target genes.
source: TEADs are the DNA binding TFs to which the TcoFs that mediate the transcriptional outcome of the Hippo signaling pathway, Yap and Taz (also known as Wwtr1), bind to, to activate expression of their target genes.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of Hippo signaling pathway.

claim: In human cancer cell lines, Vgll4 negatively regulates the transcriptional outcome of Hippo signaling by competing with Yap and Taz for TEADs.
source: Interestingly, in various human cancer cell lines, Vgll4 was shown to negatively regulate the transcriptional outcome of Hippo signaling by competing with Yap and Taz for TEADs, therefore inhibiting their function (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: The zebrafish genome codes for three members of the Vgll4 family (Vgll4a, Vgll4b, Vgll4l) and four TEADs (Tead1a, Tead1b, Tead3a, Tead3b).
source: In addition to Yap and Taz, the zebrafish genome codes for three members of the Vgll4 family (Vgll4a, Vgll4b, Vgll4l) and four TEADs (Tead1a, Tead1b, Tead3a, Tead3b).
evidence: Based on genomic information about zebrafish.

claim: Only Vgll4l, Vgll4b, Yap, Taz, Tead1a and Tead3a are expressed in KV and/or KV progenitors.
source: However, only Vgll4l, Vgll4b, Yap, Taz, Tead1a and Tead3a are expressed in KV and/or KV progenitors (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Loss of function of Vgll4l strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of function of Vgll4b strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of function of Yap strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of function of Taz strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of function of Tead1a strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of function of Tead3a strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
source: Looking at the direction of the heart jog at one day of development (Figure 1B) and at the expression of lefty1 in dorsal diencephalon (Thisse and Thisse, 1999) at 20 hr post fertilization (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) we found that loss of function of each of these TFs or TcoFs strongly disrupts embryo laterality.
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and lefty1 expression data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Specificity of knockdown phenotypes was demonstrated by their reproducibility using different non overlapping MOs and in rescue experiments through injection of MOs insensitive mRNAs.
source: Specificity of knockdown phenotypes was demonstrated by their reproducibility using different non overlapping MOs and in rescue experiments through injection of in vitro synthesized, MOs insensitive, mRNAs (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Incubation with 2.5 µM of Verteporfin, a Yap inhibitor, disrupts embryo laterality.
source: The implication of Yap in embryo laterality was further confirmed (Figure 1B) by incubating embryos in 2.5 µM of Verteporfin, a drug inducing Yap sequestration in the cytoplasm and promoting its degradation in the proteasome (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B and citation to Wang et al., 2016.

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 mutants for vgll4l, vgll4b, yap and taz were generated with insertions/deletions leading to premature stop resulting in truncated proteins lacking essential functional domains.
source: To validate our observations obtained with MO knockdowns or drug treatment, we generated CRISPR-Cas9 mutants for vgll4l, vgll4b, yap and taz. For each gene, we identified insertions/deletions (INDELs) leading to a premature stop resulting in truncated proteins lacking essential functional domains (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by schematic of mutant proteins in Figure 1C.

claim: A tead3a mutant lacking an essential splice site leading to a premature end of translation was obtained from the Zebrafish Mutation Project.
source: For tead3a, a mutant lacking an essential splice site leading to a premature end of translation was obtained from the Zebrafish Mutation Project (ZMP) (Kettleborough et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kettleborough et al., 2013.

claim: Individual homozygous mutants embryos for Tead3a, Yap, Taz, Vgll4b and Vgll4l display normal morphology at late developmental stages.
source: Whereas individual homozygous mutants embryos for Tead3a, Yap, Taz, Vgll4b and Vgll4l display normal morphology at late developmental stages (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), analysis of their laterality fully confirmed the LR asymmetry defects observed in knockdown experiments (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by images in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Analysis of laterality in homozygous mutants for Tead3a, Yap, Taz, Vgll4b and Vgll4l fully confirmed the LR asymmetry defects observed in knockdown experiments.
source: Whereas individual homozygous mutants embryos for Tead3a, Yap, Taz, Vgll4b and Vgll4l display normal morphology at late developmental stages (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), analysis of their laterality fully confirmed the LR asymmetry defects observed in knockdown experiments (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the mouse embryo, partial redundancy of Yap and Taz has been proposed to explain the weak phenotype observed in Taz mutants.
source: In the mouse embryo, partial redundancy of Yap and Taz has been proposed to explain the weak phenotype observed in Taz mutants (Miesfeld et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Miesfeld et al., 2015 and Sun et al., 2017.

claim: In fish, taz morphants and mutants show mild laterality defects.
source: In fish, whereas we observe mild laterality defects in taz morphants and mutants, these defects are much more severe in double Yap/Taz MO knockdowns (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B.

claim: Laterality defects are much more severe in double Yap/Taz MO knockdowns compared to single taz morphants and mutants.
source: In fish, whereas we observe mild laterality defects in taz morphants and mutants, these defects are much more severe in double Yap/Taz MO knockdowns (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1B.

claim: Lack of one copy of yap strongly increases the laterality defects observed in homozygous taz mutants.
source: In addition, lack of one copy of yap strongly increases the laterality defects observed in homozygous taz mutants (from 20% embryos with no heart jog or a right heart jog in single taz mutants to 55% for embryos homozygous for taz and heterozygous for yap - Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 1D.

claim: DFC clusters are present at early gastrula stage for every Hippo TF/TcoF mutant/morphant tested.
source: First, using in situ hybridization for sox17, an early DFC marker, we found that DFC clusters are present at early gastrula stage for every Hippo TF/TcoF mutant/morphant tested (not shown), strongly supporting that these factors are not required for the specification of LRO progenitors.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data for sox17.

claim: Hippo TFs/TcoFs are not required for the specification of LRO progenitors.
source: First, using in situ hybridization for sox17, an early DFC marker, we found that DFC clusters are present at early gastrula stage for every Hippo TF/TcoF mutant/morphant tested (not shown), strongly supporting that these factors are not required for the specification of LRO progenitors.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of DFC clusters in mutants/morphants.

claim: Lack of Hippo TFs/TcoFs activity has a dramatic effect on the formation of the KV with a strong decrease of its size.
source: Conversely, lack of their activity has a dramatic effect on the formation of the KV (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) with a strong decrease of its size (Figure 2E).
evidence: Supported by KV size measurements in Figure 2E and images in Figure 2A-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gain of Yap function through DFC specific injection of its mRNA results in an increase of the KV size associated with an increase in the number of KV cells.
source: In contrast, gain of Yap function through injection of its in vitro synthesized mRNA in a DFC specific manner (Esguerra et al., 2007; Matsui et al., 2011) results in an increase of the KV size associated with an increase in the number of KV cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and citations to Esguerra et al., 2007 and Matsui et al., 2011.

claim: The initial number of DFCs at early gastrula (60% epiboly) in embryos lacking Hippo TFs/TcoFs function is similar to control.
source: While the initial number of DFCs at early gastrula (60% epiboly) in embryos lacking Hippo TFs/TcoFs function is similar to control, we found a significant reduction in the DFC number at the end of gastrulation for each loss of function analyzed (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by DFC number quantification in Figure 2F.

claim: There is a significant reduction in the DFC number at the end of gastrulation for each Hippo TF/TcoF loss of function analyzed.
source: While the initial number of DFCs at early gastrula (60% epiboly) in embryos lacking Hippo TFs/TcoFs function is similar to control, we found a significant reduction in the DFC number at the end of gastrulation for each loss of function analyzed (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by DFC number quantification in Figure 2F.

claim: Measurement of the mitotic index at late gastrula stage revealed a moderate effect in Vgll4l, Yap/Taz and Tead1a knockdowns.
source: Measurement of the mitotic index at late gastrula stage revealed a moderate effect in Vgll4l, Yap/Taz and Tead1a knockdowns, while the mitotic index of the DFCs was not significantly affected in Vgll4b and Tead3a (Figure 2G).
evidence: Supported by mitotic index measurements in Figure 2G.

claim: The mitotic index of the DFCs was not significantly affected in Vgll4b and Tead3a knockdowns.
source: Measurement of the mitotic index at late gastrula stage revealed a moderate effect in Vgll4l, Yap/Taz and Tead1a knockdowns, while the mitotic index of the DFCs was not significantly affected in Vgll4b and Tead3a (Figure 2G).
evidence: Supported by mitotic index measurements in Figure 2G.

claim: Cell survival, analyzed by measuring the apoptotic index of DFCs at 80% epiboly, was affected in Hippo TFs/TcoFs loss-of-function embryos.
source: We also observed that cell survival, analyzed by measuring the apoptotic index of DFCs at 80% epiboly, was affected in Hippo TFs/TcoFs loss-of-function embryos (Figure 2H).
evidence: Supported by apoptotic index measurements in Figure 2H.

claim: In all Hippo TFs/TcoFs loss of function cases, there is a significant shortening of cilia.
source: Finally, because motile cilia are essential to the function of the LRO, we looked for their presence and measured their length in embryos lacking activity of any of Hippo TFs/TcoFs. In all cases, we found a significant shortening of cilia (Figure 3) supporting that Hippo TFs/TcoFs are required for motile ciliogenesis.
evidence: Supported by cilia length measurements in Figure 3.

claim: Hippo TFs/TcoFs are required for motile ciliogenesis.
source: Finally, because motile cilia are essential to the function of the LRO, we looked for their presence and measured their length in embryos lacking activity of any of Hippo TFs/TcoFs. In all cases, we found a significant shortening of cilia (Figure 3) supporting that Hippo TFs/TcoFs are required for motile ciliogenesis.
evidence: Inferred from the significant shortening of cilia in loss of function conditions.

claim: There are contradictory reports on the role of Hippo signaling on ciliogenesis.
source: There are contradictory reports on the role of Hippo signaling on ciliogenesis. In one study, Yap was described not to be involved in that process (Kim et al., 2014), whereas another study linked Yap to the formation of non-motile cilia during zebrafish kidney development (He et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kim et al., 2014 and He et al., 2015.

claim: Yap was described not to be involved in ciliogenesis in one study.
source: In one study, Yap was described not to be involved in that process (Kim et al., 2014), whereas another study linked Yap to the formation of non-motile cilia during zebrafish kidney development (He et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kim et al., 2014.

claim: Another study linked Yap to the formation of non-motile cilia during zebrafish kidney development.
source: In one study, Yap was described not to be involved in that process (Kim et al., 2014), whereas another study linked Yap to the formation of non-motile cilia during zebrafish kidney development (He et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to He et al., 2015.

claim: The canonical Hippo pathway is required for proper organization of motile cilia.
source: Our observations support the latter conclusion, implicating Yap in ciliogenesis and demonstrating that the canonical Hippo pathway is required for proper organization of motile cilia.
evidence: Inferred from the observations of cilia defects in Hippo TFs/TcoFs loss of function.

claim: Expression of 30% of tested DFC specific genes (24/78) was either strongly decreased or completely absent in Vgll4l depleted DFCs.
source: In a first experiment, we examined the consequences of their loss of function by MO knockdown on the expression of the 78 DFC specific genes we previously identified in high throughput in situ hybridization screens (http://zfin.org/, gene expression section). Expression of 30% of tested candidates (24/78) was either strongly decreased or completely absent in Vgll4l depleted DFCs (Figure 4).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 4.

claim: 1/3 (8/24) of genes downregulated in Vgll4l depleted DFCs are known to be required for the formation of the KV.
source: Remarkably, 1/3 (8/24) of these genes are known to be required for the formation of the KV. They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Supported by known functions of these genes and citation to Gokey et al., 2015.

claim: cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, and ttc25 are involved in cilium assembly.
source: They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Based on known functions of these genes.

claim: cftr and cldn5a are involved in KV lumen expansion.
source: They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Based on known functions of these genes.

claim: atp6ap1b is involved in proton transport that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation.
source: They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gokey et al., 2015.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is involved in DNA methylation.
source: They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Based on known function of dnmt3bb.1.

claim: ndr1 belongs to the Nodal signaling pathway.
source: They are involved in cilium assembly (cdc14aa, daw1, dnaaf4, ttc25), KV lumen expansion (cftr, cldn5a), proton transport (atp6ap1b) that has been shown to mediate DFC proliferation (Gokey et al., 2015), DNA methylation (dnmt3bb.1) or belong to the Nodal signaling pathway (ndr1).
evidence: Based on known function of ndr1.

claim: DFCs depleted for Yap/Taz display a clear decrease in expression for cdc14aa, tnfrsf21, dnaaf4, cftr or ndr1.
source: Similarly, we found that DFCs depleted for Yap/Taz display a clear decrease in expression for cdc14aa, tnfrsf21, dnaaf4, cftr or ndr1 (not shown).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data (not shown).

claim: Vgll4l and Yap/Taz regulate, directly or indirectly, the expression of genes that are essential for a variety of processes involved in the formation and function of the KV.
source: Therefore, in addition to their known function in regulating cell proliferation and survival, Vgll4l and Yap/Taz regulate, directly or indirectly, the expression of genes that are essential for a variety of processes involved in the formation and function of the KV.
evidence: Inferred from the downregulation of genes essential for KV formation in loss of function conditions.

claim: DFC specific MO knockdowns for Vgll4l and Yap result in a strong decrease of the expression of DFC specific genes in the progenitors of the LRO.
source: We investigated the tissue specificity of Vgll4l and Yap activity by performing DFC specific MO knockdowns for a subset of these 24 probes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). In all cases we observed a strong decrease of the expression of these genes in the progenitors of the LRO.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The regulation of the expression of DFC specific genes by Yap and Vgll4l is not a secondary consequence of a global loss of function affecting the whole embryo from the beginning of development but results from the activity of these TcoFs in the DFCs.
source: This shows that the regulation of the expression of DFC specific genes by Yap and Vgll4l we observed is not a secondary consequence of a global loss of function affecting the whole embryo from the beginning of development but results from the activity of these TcoFs in the DFCs.
evidence: Inferred from the DFC specific knockdown experiments.

claim: Principal Component Analysis reveals that experimental replicates for DFC transcriptomes were highly reproducible and strongly clustered.
source: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed on transcriptome data of the four replicates for each condition (Figure 5A) and reveals that experimental replicates were highly reproducible and strongly clustered.
evidence: Supported by PCA plot in Figure 5A.

claim: Each experimental condition (control, Vgll4l loss of function, Yap/Taz loss of function) segregated in distinct groups in PCA analysis.
source: Each experimental condition segregated in distinct groups pointing out that DFCs of control embryos and of embryos lacking Vgll4l or Yap/Taz have clearly distinct transcriptomes.
evidence: Supported by PCA plot in Figure 5A.

claim: DFCs of control embryos and of embryos lacking Vgll4l or Yap/Taz have clearly distinct transcriptomes.
source: Each experimental condition segregated in distinct groups pointing out that DFCs of control embryos and of embryos lacking Vgll4l or Yap/Taz have clearly distinct transcriptomes.
evidence: Inferred from the PCA analysis showing distinct clustering.

claim: There are 9215 differentially expressed genes in DFCs of embryos depleted in Vgll4l.
source: We found 9215 differentially expressed genes (DEGs: genes with normalized counts ≥ 1; |log2FoldChange| ≥ 1; Benjamini-Hochberg - False Discovery Rate - adjusted p-value<0.05) in DFCs of embryos depleted in Vgll4l and 7,925 DEGs in DFCs of embryos lacking both Yap and Taz activities (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: There are 7,925 differentially expressed genes in DFCs of embryos lacking both Yap and Taz activities.
source: We found 9215 differentially expressed genes (DEGs: genes with normalized counts ≥ 1; |log2FoldChange| ≥ 1; Benjamini-Hochberg - False Discovery Rate - adjusted p-value<0.05) in DFCs of embryos depleted in Vgll4l and 7,925 DEGs in DFCs of embryos lacking both Yap and Taz activities (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: The expression of all the 24 genes found strongly decreased in Vgll4l loss of function in in situ hybridization analysis was also significantly downregulated in the transcriptome of Vgll4l depleted DFCs.
source: As a quality control of RNA sequencing, we confirmed that the expression of all the 24 genes found strongly decreased in Vgll4l loss of function in our in situ hybridization analysis (Figure 4) was also significantly downregulated in the transcriptome of Vgll4l depleted DFCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by box plots in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: 84% (5394/6423) of overlapping DEGs for Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function are regulated similarly in DFCs (either downregulated or upregulated).
source: Analysis of the overlapping sets of DEGs for Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function (6423 genes - Figure 5B) revealed that 84% (5394/6423) of them are regulated similarly in DFCs (either downregulated or upregulated) by Vgll4l and by Yap/Taz while only 16% (1029/6423) are regulated in opposing ways (upregulated in loss of function of Vgll4l while downregulated in Yap/Taz or vice-versa).
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Only 16% (1029/6423) of overlapping DEGs for Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function are regulated in opposing ways.
source: Analysis of the overlapping sets of DEGs for Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function (6423 genes - Figure 5B) revealed that 84% (5394/6423) of them are regulated similarly in DFCs (either downregulated or upregulated) by Vgll4l and by Yap/Taz while only 16% (1029/6423) are regulated in opposing ways (upregulated in loss of function of Vgll4l while downregulated in Yap/Taz or vice-versa).
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Vgll4 in other model systems is thought to act antagonistically to Yap/Taz by competition for the binding to TEADs.
source: This is a surprising observation as Vgll4 in other model systems is thought to act antagonistically to Yap/Taz by competition for the binding to TEADs (Johnson and Halder, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Johnson and Halder, 2014.

claim: There are 318 zebrafish homologues for 380 Yap direct target genes described in mammals present within the zebrafish genome.
source: We found 318 homologues for 380 Yap direct target genes described in mammals (Lin et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2018; Zanconato et al., 2015) present within the zebrafish genome (GRCz10).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lin et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2018; Zanconato et al., 2015 and genomic analysis.

claim: Amongst 318 zebrafish homologues of mammalian Yap direct target genes, 143 were DEGs for both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz.
source: Amongst them 143 were DEGs for both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data analysis.

claim: 82.5% of zebrafish homologues of mammalian Yap direct target genes that are DEGs (118/143) are regulated similarly by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz.
source: Analysis of the transcriptome data revealed (Supplementary file 2) that 82.5% of these genes (118/143) are regulated similarly by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz (61 downregulated and 57 upregulated in morphant DFCs) while only 17.5% (25/143) are regulated in opposite ways.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data analysis in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Only 17.5% (25/143) of zebrafish homologues of mammalian Yap direct target genes that are DEGs are regulated in opposite ways by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz.
source: Analysis of the transcriptome data revealed (Supplementary file 2) that 82.5% of these genes (118/143) are regulated similarly by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz (61 downregulated and 57 upregulated in morphant DFCs) while only 17.5% (25/143) are regulated in opposite ways.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data analysis in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Most of the genes that are direct targets of Yap in mammals will also be direct targets of Yap in zebrafish.
source: It is very likely that most of the genes that are direct targets of Yap in mammals will also be direct targets of Yap in zebrafish.
evidence: Based on evolutionary conservation and homology.

claim: The similar regulation of mammalian Yap target gene homologues by Vgll4l and by Yap/Taz is strong evidence against a role of Vgll4l as a Yap antagonist during formation of the LRO in zebrafish.
source: Therefore, the similar regulation of these genes by Vgll4l and by Yap/Taz is a strong evidence against a role of Vgll4l as a Yap antagonist during formation of the LRO in zebrafish.
evidence: Inferred from the transcriptome data showing similar regulation patterns.

claim: Amongst the most prominent GO term groups for DEGs are those associated with the formation and function of the LRO: determination of LR symmetry, cilium movement, cilium organization and epithelium development.
source: Functional grouping of the GO terms based on GO hierarchy revealed that amongst the most prominent groups are those associated with the formation and function of the LRO: determination of LR symmetry, cilium movement, cilium organization and epithelium development (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by GO term analysis in Figure 5C.

claim: Mitotic cell cycle process was a GO term found for Yap/Taz DEGs.
source: In addition, mitotic cell cycle process was a GO term found for Yap/Taz while Vgll4l was associated with the GO term covalent chromatin modification, uncovering a role for this TcoF in the regulation of the expression of epigenetic factors.
evidence: Supported by GO term analysis.

claim: Vgll4l was associated with the GO term covalent chromatin modification, uncovering a role for this TcoF in the regulation of the expression of epigenetic factors.
source: In addition, mitotic cell cycle process was a GO term found for Yap/Taz while Vgll4l was associated with the GO term covalent chromatin modification, uncovering a role for this TcoF in the regulation of the expression of epigenetic factors.
evidence: Supported by GO term analysis.

claim: There are 166 genes whose loss of function has been described resulting into phenotypic defects in DFCs or in KV.
source: Amongst the 166 genes whose loss of function has been described resulting into phenotypic defects in DFCs or in KV (http://zfin.org/, phenotype section), we found 134 genes expressed in DFCs at late gastrula stage.
evidence: Based on ZFIN database information.

claim: 134 genes whose loss of function results in DFC or KV phenotypic defects are expressed in DFCs at late gastrula stage.
source: Amongst the 166 genes whose loss of function has been described resulting into phenotypic defects in DFCs or in KV (http://zfin.org/, phenotype section), we found 134 genes expressed in DFCs at late gastrula stage.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data.

claim: 62% (83/134) of genes whose loss of function results in DFC or KV phenotypic defects are downregulated in loss of function of Vgll4l.
source: Remarkably, 62% (83/134) and 50% (67/134) of these genes are respectively downregulated in loss of function of Vgll4l and Yap/Taz (Figure 5D, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 5D and data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: 50% (67/134) of genes whose loss of function results in DFC or KV phenotypic defects are downregulated in loss of function of Yap/Taz.
source: Remarkably, 62% (83/134) and 50% (67/134) of these genes are respectively downregulated in loss of function of Vgll4l and Yap/Taz (Figure 5D, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 5D and data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: 75% (46/61) of genes involved in motile ciliogenesis and associated with defects of the KV function are downregulated in Vgll4l depleted DFCs.
source: This includes 75% (46/61) of genes involved in motile ciliogenesis and associated with defects of the KV function for Vgll4l depleted DFCs and 52% (32/61) for Yap/Taz loss of function (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Supported by data in Supplementary file 4.

claim: 52% (32/61) of genes involved in motile ciliogenesis and associated with defects of the KV function are downregulated in Yap/Taz loss of function.
source: This includes 75% (46/61) of genes involved in motile ciliogenesis and associated with defects of the KV function for Vgll4l depleted DFCs and 52% (32/61) for Yap/Taz loss of function (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Supported by data in Supplementary file 4.

claim: Vgll4l and Yap/Taz play a major role in the regulation of motile ciliogenesis during the formation of the LRO.
source: Altogether, our transcriptome analysis further reinforced the conclusion that these factors play a major role in the regulation of motile ciliogenesis during the formation of the LRO.
evidence: Inferred from the high percentage of ciliogenesis genes downregulated in loss of function conditions.

claim: The molecular and cellular processes leading to the formation of a functional LRO are known to be regulated by major signaling pathways including Nodal, FGF, non-canonical Wnt and Notch.
source: The molecular and cellular processes leading to the formation of a functional LRO are known to be regulated by major signaling pathways including Nodal, FGF, non-canonical Wnt and Notch (reviewed in Matsui and Bessho, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Matsui and Bessho, 2012.

claim: There is a strong downregulation of nodal related 1 (ndr1) expression in both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function.
source: We found a strong downregulation of nodal related 1 (ndr1) expression in both Vgll4l (Figures 4C and 6A) and Yap/Taz (Figure 6A) loss of function.
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 4C and 6A.

claim: In Vgll4l loss of function, the loss of Ndr1 transcripts is associated with a strong decrease of the expression of smad2a.
source: In Vgll4l, this loss of Ndr1 transcripts is associated with a strong decrease of the expression of smad2a, a R-Smad known to transduce Nodal signaling and with a strong upregulation of the expression of two Nodal feedback antagonists, lefty1 (lft1) and lefty2 (lft2) (Agathon et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data and citation to Agathon et al., 2001.

claim: In Vgll4l loss of function, there is a strong upregulation of the expression of two Nodal feedback antagonists, lefty1 (lft1) and lefty2 (lft2).
source: In Vgll4l, this loss of Ndr1 transcripts is associated with a strong decrease of the expression of smad2a, a R-Smad known to transduce Nodal signaling and with a strong upregulation of the expression of two Nodal feedback antagonists, lefty1 (lft1) and lefty2 (lft2) (Agathon et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data and citation to Agathon et al., 2001.

claim: Both the decrease in Smad2a transcripts and the upregulation of Lft1 and Lft2 expression may disrupt the Nodal positive autoregulatory loop that is essential for the maintenance of ndr1 transcription.
source: Both the decrease in Smad2a transcripts and the upregulation of Lft1 and Lft2 expression may disrupt the Nodal positive autoregulatory loop that is essential for the maintenance of ndr1 transcription.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on known Nodal signaling mechanisms.

claim: In Yap/Taz loss of function, the strong decrease in ndr1 expression is associated with a decrease in Smad3a transcripts.
source: In Yap/Taz loss of function, the strong decrease in ndr1 expression is associated with a decrease in Smad3a transcripts, another R-Smad transducing Nodal signaling, but we did not observe an upregulation of Lft1 or Lft2 expression (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: In Yap/Taz loss of function, there is no upregulation of Lft1 or Lft2 expression.
source: In Yap/Taz loss of function, the strong decrease in ndr1 expression is associated with a decrease in Smad3a transcripts, another R-Smad transducing Nodal signaling, but we did not observe an upregulation of Lft1 or Lft2 expression (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6A.

claim: There is a strong downregulation of expression of ligand (Wnt11) and receptors (Fzd8a and Fzd10 for Vgll4l, Fzd8a for Yap/Taz) of the non-canonical Wnt pathway.
source: In addition to Nodal, the non-canonical Wnt, the FGF and the Notch pathways are also affected. We observed a strong downregulation of expression of ligand (Wnt11) and receptors (Fzd8a, Fzd10 for Vgll4l, Fzd10 for Yap/Taz) of the non-canonical Wnt pathway (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: Expression of ligands (Fgf8a and Fgf1a for Vgll4l; Fgf1a for Yap/Taz) of the FGF signaling pathway is downregulated in both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss-of-function conditions.
source: Expression of ligands (Fgf8a and Fgf1a for Vgll4l; Fgf1a for Yap/Taz) of the FGF signaling pathway is downregulated in both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss-of-function conditions and the amount of transcripts of the Fgf receptor, Fgfr1a, and of the positive Fgf feedback regulator, Cnpy1, is strongly decreased in DFCs lacking Vgll4l (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: The amount of transcripts of the Fgf receptor, Fgfr1a, and of the positive Fgf feedback regulator, Cnpy1, is strongly decreased in DFCs lacking Vgll4l.
source: Expression of ligands (Fgf8a and Fgf1a for Vgll4l; Fgf1a for Yap/Taz) of the FGF signaling pathway is downregulated in both Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss-of-function conditions and the amount of transcripts of the Fgf receptor, Fgfr1a, and of the positive Fgf feedback regulator, Cnpy1, is strongly decreased in DFCs lacking Vgll4l (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: The expression of ligands (Dla, Jag2b) and receptors (Notch1a, Notch1b and Notch3) of the Notch signaling pathway is downregulated in DFCs lacking either Vgll4l or Yap/Taz.
source: As well the expression of ligands (Dla, Jag2b) and receptors (Notch1a, Notch1b and Notch3) of the Notch signaling pathway (Figure 6D) is downregulated in DFCs lacking either Vgll4l or Yap/Taz.
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 6D.

claim: Vgll4l and Yap/Taz are essential upstream regulators of the major signaling pathways controlling the formation of the LRO.
source: Altogether, these observations provide evidence that Vgll4l and Yap/Taz are essential upstream regulators of the major signaling pathways controlling the formation of the LRO.
evidence: Inferred from the downregulation of multiple signaling pathway components in loss of function conditions.

claim: The precise temporal order by which TFs selectively activate gene expression during development is critical to ensure proper lineage commitment, cell fate determination, and ultimately organogenesis.
source: The precise temporal order by which TFs selectively activate gene expression during development is critical to ensure proper lineage commitment, cell fate determination, and ultimately organogenesis.
evidence: Based on established developmental biology knowledge.

claim: Only a small number of TFs has been shown to be necessary for the formation of the LRO.
source: So far, only a small number of TFs has been shown to be necessary for the formation of the LRO, either for the specification of its progenitors [Dharma (Fekany et al., 1999), Sox32 (Essner et al., 2005), Sox17 (Aamar and Dawid, 2010)] or for the formation and function of the KV [FoxJ1a (Yu et al., 2008), Tbx16 (Amack et al., 2007), Tbxta (Amack et al., 2007) and Rfx2 (Bisgrove et al., 2012)].
evidence: Supported by citations to Fekany et al., 1999; Essner et al., 2005; Aamar and Dawid, 2010; Yu et al., 2008; Amack et al., 2007; Bisgrove et al., 2012.

claim: Dharma, Sox32, and Sox17 are TFs necessary for the specification of LRO progenitors.
source: So far, only a small number of TFs has been shown to be necessary for the formation of the LRO, either for the specification of its progenitors [Dharma (Fekany et al., 1999), Sox32 (Essner et al., 2005), Sox17 (Aamar and Dawid, 2010)] or for the formation and function of the KV [FoxJ1a (Yu et al., 2008), Tbx16 (Amack et al., 2007), Tbxta (Amack et al., 2007) and Rfx2 (Bisgrove et al., 2012)].
evidence: Supported by citations to Fekany et al., 1999; Essner et al., 2005; Aamar and Dawid, 2010.

claim: FoxJ1a, Tbx16, Tbxta and Rfx2 are TFs necessary for the formation and function of the KV.
source: So far, only a small number of TFs has been shown to be necessary for the formation of the LRO, either for the specification of its progenitors [Dharma (Fekany et al., 1999), Sox32 (Essner et al., 2005), Sox17 (Aamar and Dawid, 2010)] or for the formation and function of the KV [FoxJ1a (Yu et al., 2008), Tbx16 (Amack et al., 2007), Tbxta (Amack et al., 2007) and Rfx2 (Bisgrove et al., 2012)].
evidence: Supported by citations to Yu et al., 2008; Amack et al., 2007; Bisgrove et al., 2012.

claim: Transcripts of sox32, sox17, tbxta, tbx16, foxj1a and rfx2 are expressed in DFCs during gastrulation.
source: However, transcripts of sox32, sox17, tbxta, tbx16, foxj1a and rfx2 are expressed in DFCs during gastrulation and we found they are all significantly downregulated in Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function (Figure 7).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data in Figure 7.

claim: sox32, sox17, tbxta, tbx16, foxj1a and rfx2 are all significantly downregulated in Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function.
source: However, transcripts of sox32, sox17, tbxta, tbx16, foxj1a and rfx2 are expressed in DFCs during gastrulation and we found they are all significantly downregulated in Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function (Figure 7).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data in Figure 7.

claim: Vgll4l and Yap/Taz act upstream of the TFs known to be essential to the formation of the LRO and are involved in the regulation of their expression.
source: These observations strongly support that Vgll4l and Yap/Taz act upstream of the TFs known to be essential to the formation of the LRO and are involved in the regulation of their expression.
evidence: Inferred from the downregulation of known LRO TFs in Vgll4l and Yap/Taz loss of function.

claim: Lineage commitment, cell fate determination and ultimately organogenesis are regulated by epigenetic mechanisms.
source: Lineage commitment, cell fate determination and ultimately organogenesis are also regulated by epigenetic mechanisms.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of developmental biology.

claim: Transcriptome analysis revealed that depletion of Vgll4l affects expression of genes involved in covalent chromatin modification.
source: Transcriptome analysis revealed that depletion of Vgll4l affects expression of genes involved in covalent chromatin modification (Figures 5C and 8).
evidence: Supported by GO term analysis in Figure 5C and gene expression data in Figure 8.

claim: In DFCs, Vgll4l loss of function leads to a strong downregulation of the expression of genes coding for the de novo DNA methyltransferases Dnmt3ba, Dnmt3bb.1, Dnmt3bb.2.
source: Indeed, in DFCs, Vgll4l loss of function leads to a strong downregulation of the expression of genes coding for writers of the DNA methylation marks: the de novo DNA methyltransferases Dnmt3ba, Dnmt3bb.1, Dnmt3bb.2 (Chédin, 2011) (Figures 4Q–R and 8) and the maintenance DNA methyltransferase Dnmt1 (Mohan and Chaillet, 2013) (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 4Q-R and 8, and citations to Chédin, 2011 and Mohan and Chaillet, 2013.

claim: In DFCs, Vgll4l loss of function leads to a strong downregulation of the expression of the maintenance DNA methyltransferase Dnmt1.
source: Indeed, in DFCs, Vgll4l loss of function leads to a strong downregulation of the expression of genes coding for writers of the DNA methylation marks: the de novo DNA methyltransferases Dnmt3ba, Dnmt3bb.1, Dnmt3bb.2 (Chédin, 2011) (Figures 4Q–R and 8) and the maintenance DNA methyltransferase Dnmt1 (Mohan and Chaillet, 2013) (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 8 and citation to Mohan and Chaillet, 2013.

claim: Vgll4l regulates the expression of the readers of DNA methylation marks, the Methyl-CpG-Binding Domain proteins: Mbd1b, Mbd2, Mbd3a, Mbd3b and Mbd6.
source: In addition we found that Vgll4l also regulates the expression of the readers of DNA methylation marks, the Methyl-CpG-Binding Domain proteins: Mbd1b, Mbd2, Mbd3a (Figure 8), Mbd3b (Figures 4S, 8) (note that while in mammals the methyl binding domain of MBD3 harbors critical mutations - K30H and Y34F - preventing it to bind to methylated DNA (Saito and Ishikawa, 2002), the methyl binding domain of Mbd3 in lower vertebrates retains the K30 and Y34 amino acids and binds to methylated DNA (Bogdanović and Veenstra, 2011) and Mbd6 (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 4S and 8, and citations to Saito and Ishikawa, 2002 and Bogdanović and Veenstra, 2011.

claim: In mammals the methyl binding domain of MBD3 harbors critical mutations - K30H and Y34F - preventing it to bind to methylated DNA.
source: note that while in mammals the methyl binding domain of MBD3 harbors critical mutations - K30H and Y34F - preventing it to bind to methylated DNA (Saito and Ishikawa, 2002), the methyl binding domain of Mbd3 in lower vertebrates retains the K30 and Y34 amino acids and binds to methylated DNA (Bogdanović and Veenstra, 2011)
evidence: Supported by citation to Saito and Ishikawa, 2002.

claim: The methyl binding domain of Mbd3 in lower vertebrates retains the K30 and Y34 amino acids and binds to methylated DNA.
source: note that while in mammals the methyl binding domain of MBD3 harbors critical mutations - K30H and Y34F - preventing it to bind to methylated DNA (Saito and Ishikawa, 2002), the methyl binding domain of Mbd3 in lower vertebrates retains the K30 and Y34 amino acids and binds to methylated DNA (Bogdanović and Veenstra, 2011)
evidence: Supported by citation to Bogdanović and Veenstra, 2011.

claim: Depletion of the de novo DNA methyltransferase, Dnmt3bb.1 has been previously shown to affect the establishment of the LR asymmetry.
source: Depletion of the de novo DNA methyltransferase, Dnmt3bb.1 has been previously shown to affect the establishment of the LR asymmetry (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: A TALEN induced mutant that affects only the catalytic site of Dnmt3bb.1 affects the establishment of the LR asymmetry.
source: We confirmed this observation with a TALEN induced mutant that affects only the catalytic site of Dnmt3bb.1.
evidence: Supported by mutant analysis.

claim: Loss of function of other de novo Dnmts expressed in DFCs (Dnmt3bb.2 and Dnmt3ba) affects the establishment of the LR asymmetry.
source: Similarly, we found that loss of function of other de novo Dnmts expressed in DFCs (Dnmt3bb.2 and Dnmt3ba) or depletion of the readers of the DNA methylation marks, Mbd3a and Mbd3b also affect the establishment of the LR asymmetry (Figure 9A).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 9A.

claim: Depletion of the readers of the DNA methylation marks, Mbd3a and Mbd3b affects the establishment of the LR asymmetry.
source: Similarly, we found that loss of function of other de novo Dnmts expressed in DFCs (Dnmt3bb.2 and Dnmt3ba) or depletion of the readers of the DNA methylation marks, Mbd3a and Mbd3b also affect the establishment of the LR asymmetry (Figure 9A).
evidence: Supported by cardiac jogging data in Figure 9A.

claim: Phenotypic analyses of KV formation in embryos depleted for Dnmt3bb.1 or Mbd3b reveals striking similarities with Vgll4l loss-of-function phenotype.
source: Phenotypic analyses of KV formation in embryos depleted for one de novo Dnmt (Dnmt3bb.1) or for one Methyl-CpG-Binding Domain protein (Mbd3b) reveals striking similarities with Vgll4l loss-of-function phenotype: reduction of KV size (Figure 9B), decreased number of DFCs at late gastrulation (Figure 9C) associated with a moderate decrease of DFC mitotic index (Figure 9D), an increased apoptotic index (Figure 9E) as well as a significant reduction in length of KV motile cilia (Figure 9F).
evidence: Supported by data in Figures 9B-F.

claim: Defects in KV organogenesis observed in Vgll4l loss of function may result, at least in part, from the decreased expression of Dnmt3bs and Mbd3s in DFCs.
source: These observations strongly support that defects in KV organogenesis observed in Vgll4l loss of function may result, at least in part, from the decreased expression of Dnmt3bs and Mbd3s in DFCs.
evidence: Inferred from the similar phenotypes of Vgll4l, Dnmt3bb.1, and Mbd3b loss of function.

claim: Laterality defects of Vgll4l loss of function can be partially rescued by gain of function of Dnmt3bb.1.
source: In strong agreement with this hypothesis, we found that laterality defects of Vgll4l loss of function can be partially rescued by gain of function of Dnmt3bb.1 (Figure 9G).
evidence: Supported by rescue experiment data in Figure 9G.

claim: There is a significant decrease in DNA methylation of DFC nuclei in both Vgll4l morphants and in homozygous vgll4l mutants.
source: We found a significant decrease in DNA methylation of DFC nuclei in both Vgll4l morphants and in homozygous vgll4l mutants (Figure 10).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence quantification in Figure 10.

claim: Vgll4l regulates epigenetic programming in LRO progenitors by controlling in the DFCs the expression of epigenetic modifying enzymes.
source: This shows that Vgll4l regulates epigenetic programming in LRO progenitors by controlling in the DFCs the expression of epigenetic modifying enzymes.
evidence: Inferred from the decreased DNA methylation in Vgll4l loss of function and the downregulation of Dnmts and Mbds.

claim: Formation of organs during embryonic development requires both epigenetic modification that restricts lineage potential and the activation of tissue specific genes during the process of cell differentiation.
source: Formation of organs during embryonic development requires both epigenetic modification that restricts lineage potential and the activation of tissue specific genes during the process of cell differentiation.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of developmental biology.

claim: The KV is the first functional organ of the zebrafish.
source: Using the formation of the first functional organ of the zebrafish, the KV, as a model system we addressed the question of the transcriptional regulation of organ formation.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of zebrafish development.

claim: The KV is a transient organ acting as the LRO in fish.
source: Because this transient organ acting as the LRO in fish is very simple and is functional in just a few hours and from a well characterized population of progenitors, this model is particularly suitable to characterize how TFs and epigenetic modification control the differentiation of a ciliated epithelium during organogenesis.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of zebrafish development.

claim: The KV was described by Kupffer in 1867.
source: Since its description by Kupffer in 1867 (Warga and Kane, 2018) the KV has been studied in much details at the cellular and molecular levels.
evidence: Supported by citation to Warga and Kane, 2018.

claim: Genetic screens have identified 166 genes to be required for KV formation and/or function.
source: Genetic screens have identified 166 genes to be required for its formation and/or function (http://zfin.org/, phenotypes, Kupffer's vesicle).
evidence: Based on ZFIN database information.

claim: Only 6 TFs (Rfx2, Foxj1a, Sox17, Sox32, Tbxta, Tbx16) have been reported to be necessary to the formation and function of the LRO prior to this study.
source: Surprisingly only 6 TFs: Rfx2, Foxj1a, Sox17, Sox32, Tbxta, Tbx16 have been reported to be necessary to the formation and function of the LRO.
evidence: Based on literature review.

claim: The Hippo signaling pathway was previously identified as a major regulator of tissue growth and organ size.
source: Strikingly, although the Hippo signaling pathway was previously identified as a major regulator of tissue growth and organ size (Johnson and Halder, 2014; Zhao et al., 2011), we discovered that the DNA binding TFs (Tead1a and Tead3a), the TcoFs mediators of the Hippo signaling pathway (Yap and Taz) as well as the TcoFs Vgll4b and Vgll4l (two factors homologous to the mammalian Vgll4 that negatively regulates the activity of Yap and Taz) are upstream regulators of the formation and function of the LRO.
evidence: Supported by citations to Johnson and Halder, 2014 and Zhao et al., 2011.

claim: Hippo TFs/TcoFs control the function of signaling pathways involved in LRO formation as well as the expression of genes essential to the formation and function of a ciliated epithelium with motile cilia.
source: These TFs and TcoFs (collectively named Hippo TFs/TcoFs thereafter in the text) control the function of signaling pathways involved in this process as well as the expression of genes essential to the formation and function of a ciliated epithelium with motile cilia.
evidence: Supported by the transcriptome and phenotypic analyses presented in the study.

claim: Vgll4l controls the expression in LRO progenitors of epigenetic factors, writers (the de novo DNA methyltransferases) and readers (Methyl-CpG binding domain proteins) of DNA methylation marks.
source: Finally, we identified that Vgll4l controls the expression in LRO progenitors of epigenetic factors, writers (the de novo DNA methyltransferases) and readers (Methyl-CpG binding domain proteins) of DNA methylation marks that we found essential for DFCs proliferation and survival as well as for the formation of motile cilia.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome and phenotypic analyses presented in the study.

claim: Writers and readers of DNA methylation marks are essential for DFCs proliferation and survival as well as for the formation of motile cilia.
source: Finally, we identified that Vgll4l controls the expression in LRO progenitors of epigenetic factors, writers (the de novo DNA methyltransferases) and readers (Methyl-CpG binding domain proteins) of DNA methylation marks that we found essential for DFCs proliferation and survival as well as for the formation of motile cilia.
evidence: Supported by phenotypic analyses of Dnmt and Mbd loss of function.

claim: Hippo TFs/TcoFs are not involved in the specification of LRO progenitors but are crucial for the regulation of their number at the end of gastrulation.
source: Hippo TFs/TcoFs are not involved in the specification of LRO progenitors but are crucial for the regulation of their number at the end of gastrulation.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of DFCs at early gastrula but reduced numbers at late gastrula in loss of function conditions.

claim: While there is an effect on proliferation and viability of DFCs, most of the KV progenitors survived past gastrulation in Hippo TFs/TcoFs loss of function.
source: However, while there is an effect on proliferation and viability of DFCs, most of the KV progenitors survived past gastrulation.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of DFCs at late gastrula despite reduced numbers.

claim: The impact of Yap/Taz, Vgll4s and TEADs on the formation of the KV is not restricted to the final number of cells available for the formation of the vesicle but they also control the formation of the epithelium of the KV as well as cilia organization and motility.
source: The impact of Yap/Taz, Vgll4s and TEADs on the formation of the KV is not restricted to the final number of cells available for the formation of the vesicle but they also control the formation of the epithelium of the KV as well as cilia organization and motility.
evidence: Inferred from the multiple phenotypic defects observed beyond cell number.

claim: During the process of differentiation of LRO progenitors, Vgll4b and Vgll4l act similarly to Yap and Taz, regulating the number of DFCs and controlling motile ciliogenesis.
source: However, during the process of differentiation of LRO progenitors, we found that Vgll4b and Vgll4l act similarly to Yap and Taz, regulating the number of DFCs and controlling motile ciliogenesis.
evidence: Supported by phenotypic and transcriptome analyses.

claim: Vgll4s do not act as antagonists of Yap/Taz activity during formation of the LRO but rather function in the same or in parallel pathways.
source: This strongly suggests that Vgll4s do not act as antagonists of Yap/Taz activity during formation of the LRO but that they rather function in the same or in parallel pathways.
evidence: Inferred from the similar regulation of genes and similar phenotypes in loss of function conditions.

claim: This study describes the first transcriptional networks during the formation of a ciliated epithelium.
source: To the best of our knowledge, our study describes the first transcriptional networks during the formation of a ciliated epithelium.
evidence: Based on literature review and the novelty of the findings.

claim: Yap/Taz and Vgll4l are master regulators of the formation and function of the LRO.
source: This observation therefore places Yap/Taz and Vgll4l upstream of these signaling pathways and strongly supports that these TcoFs are master regulators of the formation and function of the LRO.
evidence: Inferred from their upstream position in regulating multiple signaling pathways and genes essential for LRO formation.

claim: The activity of the Nodal signaling pathway has been shown to be modulated through DNA methylation of the regulatory sequences of the Nodal antagonist Lefty.
source: The activity of the Nodal signaling pathway has been shown to be modulated through DNA methylation of the regulatory sequences of the Nodal antagonist Lefty (Dai et al., 2016) (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dai et al., 2016 and Wang et al., 2017.

claim: In WT embryos, lefty genes are not expressed in the precursors of the LRO.
source: In WT embryos, lefty genes are not expressed in the precursors of the LRO.
evidence: Based on transcriptome data.

claim: Expression of lft1 and lft2 is observed in DFCs of Vgll4l morphant embryos associated with a strong reduction of ndr1 expression.
source: However, our transcriptome analysis revealed expression of lft1 and lft2 in DFCs of Vgll4l morphant embryos associated with a strong reduction of ndr1 expression (Figure 6).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data in Figure 6.

claim: In Vgll4l depleted embryos, there is strong downregulation of genes coding for the 'de novo' DNA methyltransferases that establish the initial DNA methylation pattern.
source: In these Vgll4l depleted embryos, we also found strong downregulation of genes coding for the 'de novo' DNA methyltransferases that establish the initial DNA methylation pattern (Figure 8).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data in Figure 8.

claim: Expression of Nodal is strongly downregulated in embryos devoid of Yap/Taz activity.
source: Expression of Nodal is also strongly downregulated in embryos devoid of Yap/Taz activity.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data.

claim: Expression of lft1 and lft2 is not observed in the DFCs of Yap/Taz morphant embryos.
source: However, expression of lft1 and lft2 is not observed in the DFCs of Yap/Taz morphant embryos and genes coding for Dnmts were not downregulated in Yap/Taz loss of function.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data.

claim: Genes coding for Dnmts were not downregulated in Yap/Taz loss of function.
source: However, expression of lft1 and lft2 is not observed in the DFCs of Yap/Taz morphant embryos and genes coding for Dnmts were not downregulated in Yap/Taz loss of function.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome data.

claim: ndr1 expression and activity are controlled in the DFCs by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz.
source: These observations show (1) that ndr1 expression and activity are controlled in the DFCs by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz and (2) strongly suggest that distinct mechanisms are used by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz to regulate Nodal signaling in the DFCs, with Vgll4l repressing lft1 and lft2 expression likely through a positive control of the expression of de novo DNA methyltransferases in the progenitors of the LRO.
evidence: Inferred from the downregulation of ndr1 in both loss of function conditions.

claim: Distinct mechanisms are used by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz to regulate Nodal signaling in the DFCs.
source: These observations show (1) that ndr1 expression and activity are controlled in the DFCs by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz and (2) strongly suggest that distinct mechanisms are used by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz to regulate Nodal signaling in the DFCs, with Vgll4l repressing lft1 and lft2 expression likely through a positive control of the expression of de novo DNA methyltransferases in the progenitors of the LRO.
evidence: Inferred from the different effects on lefty and Dnmt expression.

claim: Vgll4l represses lft1 and lft2 expression likely through a positive control of the expression of de novo DNA methyltransferases in the progenitors of the LRO.
source: These observations show (1) that ndr1 expression and activity are controlled in the DFCs by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz and (2) strongly suggest that distinct mechanisms are used by Vgll4l and Yap/Taz to regulate Nodal signaling in the DFCs, with Vgll4l repressing lft1 and lft2 expression likely through a positive control of the expression of de novo DNA methyltransferases in the progenitors of the LRO.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on the correlation between Dnmt downregulation and lefty upregulation.

claim: The effect of Vgll4l loss of function on DNA methylation of DFC nuclei strongly supports that Vgll4l represses lefty expression through control of Dnmt expression.
source: The effect of Vgll4l loss of function on DNA methylation of DFC nuclei strongly support this interpretation.
evidence: Supported by DNA methylation quantification data.

claim: The role of DNA methylation in chromatin modifications associated with cell differentiation has been extensively analyzed.
source: The role of DNA methylation in chromatin modifications associated with cell differentiation has been extensively analyzed.
evidence: Based on established knowledge of epigenetics.

claim: The upstream regulation of DNA methylation in chromatin modifications is far less understood.
source: However, the upstream regulation of this process is far less understood.
evidence: Based on literature review.

claim: Vgll4l is required in the progenitors of the LRO for the expression of epigenetic factors, writers (the de novo DNA methyltransferase 3) and readers (Methyl-CpG binding domain proteins) of DNA methylation marks.
source: Our study reveals that one transcription cofactor, Vgll4l, is required in the progenitors of the LRO for the expression of epigenetic factors, writers (the de novo DNA methyltransferase 3) and readers (Methyl-CpG binding domain proteins) of DNA methylation marks.
evidence: Supported by transcriptome and phenotypic analyses.

claim: Vgll4l regulates epigenetics in a temporal and spatial manner by affecting the expression of some of its major actors.
source: The demonstration that Vgll4l regulates epigenetics in a temporal and spatial manner by affecting the expression of some of its major actors opens a new field of exploration for the understanding of the regulation of gene expression during cell differentiation.
